name: cadcraft
description: Make and edit CAD drawings (DXF, DWG) with CADCraft, an open-source CAD engine, in a folder you choose.
long_description: CADCraft makes new drawings from a description (layers, lines, polylines, circles, arcs, text, dimensions, hatches, blocks) and opens, inspects, edits, renders and saves DXF and DWG drawings with AutoCAD-style commands. It opens drawings from anywhere on this computer (and finds a file you drop into the chat by its name), but every file it writes goes into the working folder you choose, and it never replaces a file there: edits are saved under new names.

working_folder.title: Working folder
working_folder.description: The folder new drawings are saved to. CADCraft can open and save drawings anywhere on this computer. Made on first use if it doesn't exist.

tools.name: command_line
tools.description: Type one line at the CADCraft command line, exactly as a user would at an AutoCAD-style prompt. Starts commands by name or alias (LINE, L, CIRCLE, C, PLINE, RECTANG, MOVE, TRIM, OFFSET, ZOOM…) and answers the active prompt: points `x,y`, relative `@dx,dy`, polar `@dist<angle`, distances, keywords (e.g. `c` for Close), empty text = Enter. Spaces act as Enter, so `circle 0,0 5` works in one call. Returns the new prompt and command-line output, and `error` when the line was refused.

tools.name: script
tools.description: Run a multi-line script (like an AutoCAD .scr file): one or more inputs per line, blank line = Enter.

tools.name: execute
tools.description: Run any command with JSON parameters (no prompts or dialogs). Use list_commands to find ids and parameter docs. Examples: line {points:[[0,0],[10,0]]}, circle {center:[0,0], radius:5}, layer.new {name:"Walls", color:"red", current:true}, move {handles:["10A"], delta:[5,0]}, zoom {mode:"extents"}.

tools.name: list_commands
tools.description: List commands with ids, labels, menu paths, aliases and parameter docs. Optional filter: a substring of the command id, label or an alias.

tools.name: inspect_drawing
tools.description: Summary of the active drawing: entity counts, extents, layers, styles, blocks, layouts, selection, undo history and (optionally) entities with handles and geometry.

tools.name: query_entities
tools.description: Entities filtered by type (Line, Circle, Polyline…), layer, current selection (selected:true; active space only) and/or a window [[x0,y0],[x1,y1]] (objects whose geometry is inside or crosses it; crossing:false = entirely inside). Returns count (all matches), returned (this page) and entities; page with offset and limit (default 500).

tools.name: render
tools.description: Render the active drawing to a PNG and return it as an image content block (content[0].type is "image", not text): fitted to the extents by default, or just the area `window` [[x0,y0],[x1,y1]] (drawing units), e.g. one sheet or one room of a large drawing. With a window and no size the image is 1600 px wide with the window's shape. `background`: "dark" (the canvas; the default without a plot style), "white" (the default with one, as a plot prints on paper), "paper" or "#rrggbb"; colour 7 is drawn white on a dark background and black on a light one, as on a plot. `plot_style`: a plot style table, e.g. "monochrome.ctb" (every colour black, as most plots) or "grayscale.ctb", which make light colours readable on white; "none" (or "") draws every object with its own properties, also in a layout that shows its own plot styles (without `plot_style` such a layout draws with its table, as on screen). An unknown background or plot style is refused.

tools.name: find_text
tools.description: Read the drawing's texts: TEXT, MTEXT (formatting removed), block attributes and multileaders, each with its text, insertion point `at`, height, rotation, style, layer and handle. Filter by `contains` (any case), `layer` and/or `window` [[x0,y0],[x1,y1]] around the insertion points; page with offset and limit (default 200). Use it to find room names, sheet titles and notes without reading all the geometry.

tools.name: new_drawing
tools.description: Create a new drawing (imperial by default, or metric).

tools.name: open
tools.description: Open a DXF or DWG drawing with CADCraft. When the user attaches a drawing, its absolute path is provided in context: open that exact path, inspect and edit what was asked, save under a new name, then call file_attach so the user can download it. If it isn't on this computer's disk (a drawing dropped into a desktop app's chat), find it with find_files when that tool is offered; a small file you can't reach by path can be sent as `data` (base64) with its `name`. Never write Python or other code to create, read or edit a drawing. The reply lists `warnings`: what reading left out; tell the user about them.

tools.name: find_files
tools.description: Find files on this computer by name (any case, part of the name is enough), newest first, with their absolute paths. When the user attaches or drops a drawing into the chat, the file isn't on this computer's disk: search for its name here, then open the path found. Searches the working folder, Desktop, Downloads, Documents and the home folder unless `folder` is given.

tools.name: save
tools.description: Save the drawing (DXF or DWG by extension). A .svg, .png or .pdf path exports instead: the drawing keeps its name and unsaved changes. In a working folder (--root) an existing file is never replaced: save under a new name, and a save without a path writes an unused name beside the opened drawing (`plan (2).dxf`). Then call file_attach with the saved path.

tools.name: drawing_create
tools.description: Make a new, editable CAD drawing (.dxf recommended, or .dwg) in one call from structured JSON, and attach it for download. Give units, layers (name, color, linetype, lineweight), optional blocks, and entities: line, polyline, rectangle, circle, arc, text, mtext, dimension (linear, aligned, radius, diameter), hatch (a closed boundary and a pattern) and insert (of a block). Text and dimension sizes follow a plot scale chosen to fit an A3 sheet (or `scale`). The file gets an unused name if the path is taken. Never write Python or other code to create, read or edit a drawing. Returns a JSON summary (with anything `dropped`) and the file. To edit it later, open its path.

tools.name: file_attach
tools.description: Give the user a file a tool wrote, as a download: a .dwg, .dxf, .pdf, .svg, .png, .jpeg, .csv, .txt, .docx, .xlsx or .pptx file in the working folder, up to 32 MiB. Returns a short note and the file as an embedded resource.

tools.name: cancel
tools.description: Press Escape: cancel the running command (or clear the selection).
